_comment: Node.js Bot Egg — import via Admin > Nests > Import Egg
name: Node.js Bot (Git Deploy)
author: wamitiantony297@gmail.com
description: Generic Node.js bot runner. Pulls source from a Git repo (or uses uploaded files), runs npm install against package.json, and starts a chosen JS file — same behaviour as bot-hosting.net's Node.js egg.
startup: if [[ "${AUTO_UPDATE}" == "1" ]] && [[ -d .git ]]; then git pull; fi; if [[ ! -z "${NODE_PACKAGES}" ]]; then /usr/local/bin/npm install ${NODE_PACKAGES}; fi; if [[ ! -z "${UNNODE_PACKAGES}" ]]; then /usr/local/bin/npm uninstall ${UNNODE_PACKAGES}; fi; if [ -f /home/container/package.json ]; then /usr/local/bin/npm install; fi; if [[ ! -z "${START_BASH_FILE}" ]]; then bash ${START_BASH_FILE}; else /usr/local/bin/node /home/container/${BOT_JS_FILE}; fi;

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Node.js Bot Egg - installation script
# Runs once in a temporary Debian container before first boot.

apt update -y
apt install -y git curl ca-certificates

cd /mnt/server || exit 1

if [[ "${USER_UPLOADED_FILES}" == "1" ]]; then
    echo "USER_UPLOADED_FILES=1 -- skipping git clone, expecting files to be uploaded manually via SFTP/file manager."
else
    if [[ -z "${GIT_REPO_ADDRESS}" ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: GIT_REPO_ADDRESS is empty and USER_UPLOADED_FILES is not 1. Nothing to deploy."
        exit 1
    fi

    REPO_URL="${GIT_REPO_ADDRESS}"

    # Inject auth into the URL if a username + token were provided (private repos)
    if [[ ! -z "${GIT_USERNAME}" ]] && [[ ! -z "${GIT_ACCESS_TOKEN}" ]]; then
        REPO_URL=$(echo "${GIT_REPO_ADDRESS}" | sed "s#https://#https://${GIT_USERNAME}:${GIT_ACCESS_TOKEN}@#")
    fi

    echo "Cloning ${GIT_REPO_ADDRESS} ..."

    if [[ -z "${INSTALL_BRANCH}" ]]; then
        git clone "${REPO_URL}" .
    else
        git clone --branch "${INSTALL_BRANCH}" "${REPO_URL}" .
    fi
fi

if [[ -f /mnt/server/package.json ]]; then
    echo "Found package.json, dependencies will be installed on first boot."
else
    echo "No package.json found at repo root -- that's fine if your bot has no npm dependencies."
fi

echo "Install script complete."

variables.name: Git Repo Address
variables.description: GitHub repo to clone, e.g. https://github.com/youruser/your-bot-repo

variables.name: Install Branch
variables.description: The branch of the bot to install. Leave blank for the repo's default branch.

variables.name: User Uploaded Files
variables.description: Skip all the install stuff if you are letting a user upload files. 0 = false (default) 1 = true

variables.name: Auto Update
variables.description: Pull the latest files on startup when using a GitHub repo.

variables.name: Bot JS File
variables.description: The file that starts the bot.

variables.name: Additional Node Packages
variables.description: Install additional node packages. Use spaces to separate.

variables.name: Uninstall Node Packages
variables.description: Uninstall node packages. Use spaces to separate.

variables.name: Git Access Token
variables.description: Password to use with git. It's best practice to use a Personal Access Token.

variables.name: Start Bash File
variables.description: Specify a custom bash file to be run when starting the server. Git pulls and package installs will still run first.
